rationale: Section 12 is materially one-sided and fails the fallback. TrueLink's indemnity (12(b), p0073/p0075) is limited to its own breach of the Agreement or failure to perform, with no third-party intellectual-property infringement indemnity anywhere in the document (the only infringement references are Client-side warranties in 8e and the domain-name search obligation in 2h), and no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies. We therefore target the preferred position: an express TrueLink duty to defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates for third-party IP, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct claims with notice, defence control and cooperation, and Client's indemnity narrowed to Client Content and Client's breach of law. We would accept the fallback (IP-only indemnity with customary exclusions, remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap) if TrueLink resists.

verification.notes: Fallback is position-complete: the single edited sentence makes the cap mutual and aggregate, retains the existing 12-month hosting-and-support compensation basis, and places indemnification (Section 12), confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap. Preferred is not complete: missing the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable" wording and the "event giving rise to the claim" anchor; no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion; no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or infringement of the other party's IP; and no statement that Client's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. To reach preferred, the drafter must add these in operative text, not in the comment. Minimality holds: only the capped-party reference, the aggregate/scope wording and the carve-out parenthetical were touched. Deleting the "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" cross-reference was necessary rather than cosmetic — those sections do not exist, so the retained trigger was undefined and no true aggregate mutual cap could exist while it stood. Intent is preserved: the 12-month compensation measure, the existing gross negligence/wilful misconduct exception and the surrounding indemnity architecture survive; the edit removes (rather than creates) a dangling cross-reference and adds no survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories. Noted for the drafter's awareness (not a defect at fallback): the indemnity carve-out is scoped to "THIS SECTION 12" — confirm no indemnity obligations sit outside Section 12, otherwise broaden to "a party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement".

verification.notes: All six preferred elements are met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment: the Client-side affiliate and M&A successor carve-out, the Vendor-side consent requirement with a reasonableness standard, the absolute competitor bar, and the express no-termination-on-change-of-control sentence. The fallback is not met (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, and Client's other assignments no longer require consent), but position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, which is the higher position and the one claimed. Deleting the old mutual "financially responsible affiliate" exception was necessary, not gratuitous: the preferred checklist requires that Vendor may not assign without Client's consent, and any retained no-consent Vendor exception would have defeated that element. Splitting the single mutual sentence into two directional sentences is the ordinary way to render that asymmetry, so the restructure is minimal. No extras were added: no survival tail, no notice procedure, no damages or expense language, no broad notwithstanding override, and no duplicated operative term. The change-of-control sentence is a concise insertion filling a genuine gap (the original document contains no change-of-control or deemed-assignment language). Intent is preserved: the section heading and the assign-or-transfer subject matter survive, no defined term is orphaned, no cross-reference dangles, and no retained sentence contradicts the new text (the old mutual prohibition was replaced wholesale rather than left standing alongside the new permissions). Note for the drafter (not a defect against this checklist): the rewrite also drops the former approval requirement on Client's own non-affiliate, non-successor assignments. That is broader than the preferred position but is a by-product of the necessary directional split and removes only a restriction on us, so it is not treated as a minimality or intent failure; if TrueLink objects, the clean fallback ask is a mutual successor right on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Client, so it sits at our preferred position. Section 2(a) grants Client only a non-exclusive licence and expressly confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret" for similar software and services (subject only to TrueLink's IP and Section 10 confidentiality). The only sourcing-style covenant, Section 3(i) ("Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface"), is conditioned on Client's voluntary use of the Interface and therefore is not exclusivity given the express freedom to use alternatives. The Section 8(d) reference to the Non-Competition Agreement restricts TrueLink's use of Credit Data rather than binding Client's procurement, and the "solely and exclusively" language in Section 12 is a forum provision, not exclusive dealing. No redline required.

Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "damages", "fee", and dollar amounts return only ordinary compensation terms: the Section 5 minimum monthly amounts ("but not less than $____ per month") are consideration for services actually provided during the term, not a sum payable on termination or on breach, and Exhibits A and B contain only charges for services. quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
rationale: "Client" is defined as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone (p0003), so the § 2(a) grant reaches neither Client's affiliates nor contractors, and there is no notice mechanic to add affiliates. Section 15 (p0080) bars any transfer of rights without TrueLink's prior written approval, with the only exception being an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate, so the licence is not transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction. Both fallback elements therefore fail. We target the fallback: affiliates covered on written notice in the grant, and a Client-only carve-out from the assignment consent for transfer of the licence to an M&A successor (drafted as an exception rather than a "notwithstanding" override, to avoid conflict with the retained consent mechanic). We have not pressed the preferred perpetual/irrevocable and contractor points, given the subscription-style term in § 2(c).

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete: affiliate coverage on written notice is inserted directly into the § 2(a) grant, and a Client-only M&A-successor carve-out is added to the § 15 consent requirement. The finding is properly scored as a deviation because the unedited clause failed both fallback elements (no affiliate path, and all transfers of rights required TrueLink's approval). Preferred level fails on contractors (no reference added), on the paid-up perpetual/irrevocable elements (cannot be assessed; § 2(c) term/fee text not supplied and no perpetuity or irrevocability wording inserted), on the material-breach-only termination limit (no such restriction anywhere), and on general successor transferability (the carve-out is confined to merger/acquisition successors). To reach the preferred level the drafter would need to add "and its contractors acting on its behalf" to the grant, state that paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, limit revocation/termination of the subscription licence to uncured material breach, and broaden the § 15 carve-out from "a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction" to "any successor to Client's business or assets". Minimality holds: only two surgical insertions were made, both inside the target elements. No survival tail, expense language, procedure, or boilerplate was added; the pre-existing Customer-favourable non-exclusivity/free-to-use-alternatives sentence and the mutual affiliate assignment exception are retained untouched. The retained mutual affiliate exception would defeat the ASSIGN fallback, but that is a different rule and is not a LICENSE defect. No duplicate affiliate coverage arises because "Client" is defined as a single named entity. Intent is preserved: the successor right is implemented as a Client-only exception rather than a new Vendor assignment exception or a broad "notwithstanding" override, so the consent mechanic, its mutuality, and all other commercial terms survive without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created. Drafting nit (not a failure): after inserting "and, upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates", the antecedent of "its business" in "in the ordinary course of its business" is slightly ambiguous; consider "in the ordinary course of their respective businesses" for clarity. Also consider defining or lower-casing "affiliates" consistently, since the agreement uses "affiliate" in § 15 without a definition.

quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Client, so the rule sits at the preferred position. Section 2(a) (p0022/p0024) grants only a non-exclusive licence and affirmatively confirms Client is not obligated to use the Interface and is free to acquire, develop, licence or otherwise use competing software and services (subject only to TrueLink IP non-infringement and existing confidentiality obligations, which are ordinary IP/confidentiality terms, not competitive restraints). Client's covenants in §8 (compliance, notification, access limitation, spamming) contain no restraint on the businesses Client may operate or the products it may buy or build. The credit-report sourcing sentence in §3(i) (p0042) applies only where Client voluntarily requests underwriting approval "through a System using the Interface" and, read with the express freedom in §2(a), is not an exclusivity or field-of-use restriction. The "Non-Competition Agreement" referenced at §8(d) (p0054) is invoked solely as a limitation on the licence Client grants TrueLink to use Credit Data — i.e., it constrains Vendor and benefits us — so it is not flagged. No redline proposed.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional election to terminate the Agreement on written notice, with service continuing only to the last day of the month following the notice month - i.e. roughly 30 to 60 days' run-off. That is a Customer convenience right on notice no longer than the 60-90 day fallback window (and close to the 30-day preferred standard), and it is unconditional, so no cause or Vendor consent is needed. No early-termination fee, penalty or accelerated minimum payment is imposed on that election anywhere in the Agreement, so the fallback three-month fee cap is satisfied by there being no fee at all. TrueLink has no mid-term convenience termination right: the only Vendor-side exit is the 30-day notice of intent not to renew at the end of each one-year period (p0078), which is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term and is a RENEWAL-rule item, not a T4C convenience right (the Section 2/3 cut-offs in p0078 are cause-based). The term is one year, not a multi-year commitment, so the walk-away test is not engaged. Two points short of preferred are noted rather than flagged: there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (fees are invoiced monthly and paid within 15 days of receipt under p0045, so nothing is prepaid), and the run-off can exceed 30 days depending on the notice date. We also note that Section 14 is expressed as "Subject to Section 4 hereof" and Section 4 is not included in the text supplied; if Section 4 contains a minimum-commitment or accelerated-payment mechanic we would revisit. On the material terms visible, this clause sits at or above the fallback position and we would not redline it.

We reviewed the compensation provisions (§ 5-6), the licence and hosting terms (§ 2-4), and Client's covenants (§ 8), and found no obligation on Client to offer TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, to disclose third-party terms, or to match any third-party offer. quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
rationale: There is a minimum commitment on us — Section 5(a) sets monthly floor fees ("not less than $____ per month") for Hosting and Support Services, referred to again as the "minimum monthly fees" in the documentation/disputes clause (p0047). It sits at the fallback, not the preferred position, so we do not redline it. (1) Commitment period: the Agreement runs for an initial 1-year term and renews only in successive one-year periods, with either party able to give notice of non-renewal 30 days before year end (p0078), so the commitment never extends beyond the current 12-month term. (2) Exit: Section 14 gives us an unconditional election to terminate — TrueLink continues services only "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement" (p0079) — so the floor fees can be shed at will with roughly a month's notice; this is a minor variance from the fallback's clean 30-day reduction right (the effective date can fall up to ~60 days out) and we note it rather than flag it. (3) No shortfall penalty, liquidated damages or early-termination charge exists anywhere in the document; the floor is a monthly fee only, so nothing punitive needs converting to a true-up. This is therefore not walk-away territory (no multi-year take-or-pay without exit), and the minimums are in any event unfilled blanks to be completed commercially. Separately, the credit-report ordering obligation in Section 3(i) applies only where we voluntarily route an underwriting request through the Interface, and Section 2(a) expressly leaves us free to use alternative systems, so it is not a minimum purchase or volume commitment; the storage and bandwidth figures in Section 3(a)/(c) are service specifications, not usage caps with penalties.

verification.notes: Finding status "deviation" is correct: the only pre-existing TrueLink warranty (Section 9) is a Y2K date-processing warranty, and Sections 3/4 impose only "reasonable commercial efforts," so before the edit no fallback element was met (no software-to-documentation warranty, no services warranty period, no repair/replace/refund remedy). All four fallback elements are met in operative language by the single inserted sentence pair; the fallback level is position-complete. Preferred level is incomplete: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, 90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 days rather than 90 days for services, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no malicious-code warranty. The drafter must add those five items in operative text to reach the preferred position. Minimality holds: a concise insertion into the existing Section 9 for a missing clause, no deletion or paraphrase of existing text, no survival tail, no procedural or expense boilerplate, and the pre-existing Y2K warranty and its Client-favourable "at TrueLink's sole cost and expense" language are retained. The disclaimer at p0076 is already prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so correctly no carve-out edit was made. Note (not a minimality failure): the remedy is drafted "at Client's election" whereas the playbook model language gives the choice "at Vendor's option." The checklist element is silent on who elects, so this stays within the element, but it is a more aggressive posture than the model and is the likely negotiation give if TrueLink pushes back. Note (not an element failure): the services warranty is measured against "the requirements of this Agreement," and those requirements are themselves only "reasonable commercial efforts" in Sections 3 and 4, so the 30-day services warranty adds limited substantive teeth. If more bite is wanted, anchor it to the professional-and-workmanlike standard (which would also close a preferred-level gap). Intent preserved: the Y2K warranty, its evidence/repair mechanic, and the disclaimer survive without contradiction; "Interface," "Hosting Services" and "Support Services" are defined terms and no cross-reference is left dangling.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant even though TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes Client and credit data, so we have added a short insurance section at our preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request). ops.text: INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; where TrueLink processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by law. TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance upon Client's request.

verification.notes: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant anywhere (Sections 13–30 and the charges-only exhibits), so a concise insertion is the correct treatment for a 'missing' finding; all new words are necessary to build the clause. All six preferred elements appear in operative language with the correct amounts, bases (per occurrence / aggregate) and party direction (TrueLink as insuring party, Client as beneficiary of certificates). The cyber trigger is drafted broadly ('any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client'), satisfying the requirement that the Customer Data insurance trigger cover every category of Client data rather than selected named types. Minimality holds: the drafter omitted the model language's 'at its own expense' and the one-year survival tail, added no procedures, notice mechanics, additional-insured or waiver-of-subrogation extras, and deleted nothing from the retained text (Section 30 force majeure is reproduced verbatim). Intent is preserved: the insertion sits after the final section, creates no undefined term, no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict any retained allocation, remedy or timing provision.
